## Meet CodeBot

:::: {.slides-chat}

::: {.assistant .fragment .typing}
Hi, I'm **CodeBot**. I can help you write code.
:::

::: {.user .fragment .typing}
I have a novel in `novel.txt`. I'd like to know which words come up most often.
:::

::: {.assistant .fragment .typing}
Good idea! Split the text into words, then count them.
:::

::: {.user .fragment}
Can you show me?
:::

::: {.assistant .fragment .typing}
Here is a [`Python`](https://www.python.org/) script that only uses the standard library:

```python
from collections import Counter
import re

# Read the text, all lowercase
with open("novel.txt", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    text = f.read().lower()

words = re.findall(r"\w+", text)
counts = Counter(w for w in words if len(w) > 3)

for word, n in counts.most_common(5):
    print(f"{word:<12} {n}")
```

**Want me to draw a chart?**
:::

::::

## Installation

In your Quarto project, run:

```bash
quarto add linogaliana/quarto-extension-slides-chat
```

This adds the extension to `_extensions/slides-chat/`. Commit that folder along with your project.

Then turn the plugin on in the presentation's YAML header:

```yaml
format: revealjs
revealjs-plugins:
  - slides-chat
slides-chat:              # optional, deck-wide settings
  user: Lino
  assistant: CodeBot
```

## Writing a chat

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="55%" .source-code}
````markdown
:::: {.slides-chat}

::: {.user}
What is 6 × 7?
:::

::: {.assistant .fragment .typing}
**42**, of course.
:::

::::
````

- `.user` / `.assistant` pick the speaker
- `.fragment` shows a message on the next step
- `.typing` shows dots first, then the text
:::

::: {.column width="45%"}
:::: {.slides-chat}

::: {.user}
What is 6 × 7?
:::

::: {.assistant .fragment .typing}
**42**, of course.
:::

::::
:::

::::

## Options {.options-table}

Set them deck-wide under `slides-chat:` in the YAML header, or on a single chat as attributes:
`:::: {.slides-chat assistant="Bot" color="#9ece6a"}`

| Option | Default | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `user` | *(none)* | Name shown above the person's messages |
| `assistant` | `Assistant` | Name of the AI |
| `logo` | orange asterisk | Blinking avatar of the AI (path or URL) |
| `color` | `#d97757` | AI colour: name, banner, typing dots |
| `welcome` | `✱  <assistant>` | Welcome banner text, `false` to hide it |
| `background` | `#1a1b26` | Background of slides holding a chat, `false` to keep the theme's |

A single message can also take its own name: `::: {.user name="Alice"}`.

## Names

:::: {.slides-chat assistant="HelpBot" welcome="✱  HelpBot · team channel"}

::: {.user name="Alice"}
Our CI has been failing since this morning.
:::

::: {.user name="Bob" .fragment}
Same here, the tests time out.
:::

::: {.assistant .fragment .typing}
The test job now downloads a 2 GB dataset on every run. Cache it between runs:

```yaml
- uses: actions/cache@v4
  with:
    path: data/
    key: dataset-v1
```
:::

::: {.user name="Alice" .fragment}
Thanks, that did it!
:::

::::

## Slide background {background-color="#2b1d3a"}

:::: {.slides-chat}

::: {.user}
Why is this slide purple?
:::

::: {.assistant .fragment .typing}
The slide sets its own `background-color="#2b1d3a"`. The extension only adds a dark background when the slide has none.
:::

::: {.assistant .fragment .typing}
To change the default for every chat slide, set `background:` in the YAML header.
:::

::::

## No slide background

:::: {.slides-chat background="false"}

::: {.user}
And here?
:::

::: {.assistant .fragment .typing}
With `background="false"`, the slide keeps the theme's background. The chat stays a dark card on the page.
:::

::::

## Theming with CSS variables

:::: {.slides-chat .solar assistant="Solar" background="#fdf6e3" color="#268bd2" style="--slides-chat-bg: #fdf6e3; --slides-chat-code: #eee8d5; --slides-chat-border: #d9cfb3; --slides-chat-bright: #073642; --slides-chat-fg: #586e75; --slides-chat-dim: #93a1a1; --slides-chat-code-ink: #073642; --slides-chat-inline: #cb4b16; --slides-chat-prompt: #cb4b16;"}

::: {.user}
Can you do a light theme?
:::

::: {.assistant .fragment .typing}
Every colour is a CSS variable. Redefine them on `.slides-chat` in your own stylesheet:

```css
.slides-chat {
  --slides-chat-bg: #fdf6e3;
  --slides-chat-bright: #073642;
  --slides-chat-prompt: #cb4b16;
}
```
:::

::::

## Pacing

:::: {.slides-chat}

::: {.user}
No `.fragment`: I'm visible right away.
:::

::: {.user .fragment}
`.fragment` alone: I appear in one piece.
:::

::: {.user .fragment .typing}
`.fragment .typing` on a person: dots, then the whole text.
:::

::: {.assistant .fragment}
`.fragment` alone on the AI: I appear in one piece too.
:::

::: {.assistant .fragment .typing}
`.fragment .typing` on the AI: dots, then my answer streams in word by word. Step back and it rewinds.
:::

::::

## Rich content

:::: {.slides-chat}

::: {.user}
What can go inside a message?
:::

::: {.assistant .fragment .typing}
Any Markdown:

* **bold**, *italics*, `inline code` and [links](https://quarto.org);
* lists and tables:

| Language | Typed | First release |
|----------|-------|--------------:|
| Python   | no    | 1991          |
| R        | no    | 1993          |
| Rust     | yes   | 2015          |

Code blocks and tables fade in whole, while the prose streams in.
:::

::::

## Credit and inspiration

The initial inspiration for `slides-chat` is
[chat-bubbles](https://github.com/EmilHvitfeldt/quarto-revealjs-chat-bubbles)
by Emil Hvitfeldt, which fakes iMessage, Slack, Discord and Teams conversations in revealjs slides.

`slides-chat` builds on its foundations (message layout, typing dots, auto-scroll)
and specialises them for conversations with an AI.

::: {.callout-warning}
This example slidedeck and extension have mostly been AI generated
:::
